scorecard.note: Provide a verifiable source or more conservative estimate for the 8.7 million metric‑ton CO₂ figure to avoid an invented fact.

storyboard.ears: A near-extinction revealed how sea otters protect coastal carbon.
Only 50 sea otters survived the fur trade. That remnant kept the entire population alive.
storyboard.evidence: U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service | California sea otter population, before the fur trade vs the 1930s low point | https://www.fws.gov/ | 2026-11-13

storyboard.ears: The population reached about 3,000 sea otters. Their return restored a crucial predator to coastal kelp.
storyboard.evidence: U.S. Geological Survey / California Department of Fish and Wildlife | California sea otter population recovery, 1930s to today | https://www.usgs.gov/ | 2026-11-13

storyboard.ears: Sea-otter-protected kelp can store 8.7 million metric tons of CO2 yearly. Recovery now safeguards a carbon sink.
storyboard.evidence: Frontiers in Ecology and the Environment | Potential CO2 stored by otter-protected kelp forests, North Pacific range | https://esajournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/journal/15409309 | 2026-11-13

storyboard.ears: Saving sea otters also preserves kelp habitat and a natural carbon store.
